summary.oneLiner: A 52-year-old multi-brand Indian hosiery and apparel company (innerwear, outerwear, athleisure, thermals, rainwear) with ~15% share of the Indian hosiery market and one of the industry's widest distribution networks.
summary.business: Dollar Industries Limited, founded in 1972, has grown into a leading Indian hosiery and apparel company manufacturing and selling innerwear, outerwear, athleisure, thermals, rainwear and comfortwear for men, women and children under a multi-brand portfolio (Dollar Man, Dollar Woman, Dollar Junior, Force NXT, Pepe Jeans innerwear JV, among others). Products reach consumers through general trade, large-format stores, exclusive brand outlets, e-commerce, quick-commerce and exports to 15 countries, serving both B2B (dealers, distributors, wholesalers, retailers, institutions) and B2C customers.

currentContext.strengths: Backward integration from fibre to fashion across yarn, fabric and elastic manufacturing, giving control over quality, cost and input volatility and reducing vendor dependence.|Multi-brand portfolio spanning value-led everyday essentials (Dollar Always, Dollar Man) to premium/lifestyle lines (Force NXT, Pepe Jeans innerwear JV), enabling participation across price points, seasons and lifestyles.|Pan-India distribution network of 1,500+ dealers, 145,000+ retail outlets, 1,024 large-format-store presence and 1,500+ dark-store presence via quick-commerce platforms - one of the widest in the industry.|Brand ambassador equity (Akshay Kumar - Bigboss, Saif Ali Khan - Lehar, Yami Gautam - Missy, Mahesh Babu - Bigboss South India) supporting consumer recall across regions and demographics.|Project Lakshya distribution-intelligence programme (retailer mapping, digital enrolment, geo-tagging, distributor tracking) shifting the Company from a push-led to a replenishment-led, demand-responsive distribution system; covers 319 Lakshya distributors contributing 30.4% of revenue across 14 states.
currentContext.strategies: Project Lakshya: shift from a push-led to a replenishment-led, demand-responsive distribution system, supported by a stronger digital backbone (distributor visibility, retailer-level insights, inventory planning, dashboard-based reporting).|Premiumisation and portfolio relevance: strengthen higher-margin, value-added categories (Bigboss, Missy, Force NXT, athleisure, thermals) while keeping scale categories (Dollar Always, Dollar Man) strong.|Force NXT and the Pepe Jeans innerwear alliance (with G.O.A.T) to support premium and D2C ambitions, giving a differentiated route to market and digital-first consumer engagement.|Proposed merger/consolidation of promoter-group entities into Dollar Industries Limited to bring brand ownership, manufacturing/job-work arrangements and operating real estate under the listed entity, reducing related-party transactions and simplifying governance.|Balance-sheet discipline: improve free cash flow and reduce debt while supporting growth without major near-term capex commitments.|Sustainability integration: backward integration, renewable energy initiatives, responsible processing and resource efficiency to support both operating resilience and ESG priorities.|Brand building via integrated marketing campaigns across television, digital, outdoor and retail touch points, plus celebrity brand ambassadors, to strengthen retail visibility and consumer recall.|Strengthen distribution and market reach by deepening retail relationships, improving supply-chain efficiencies and leveraging technology-driven processes.|Grow international business by strengthening relationships with international distributors/partners and exploring new overseas market prospects.|FY2026-27 priorities: profitable revenue growth, margin expansion, distribution strengthening and disciplined execution of transformational initiatives under Project Lakshya; continued premiumisation, improved product mix, strengthened under-served geographies, deeper distributor engagement, and investment in technology, data-led decision-making and sales-force effectiveness; continued focus on capacity utilisation, productivity improvement and operational excellence.|Board recommended a dividend of Rs 3/- per equity share of Rs 2/- face value (150% on paid-up value), unchanged from the previous year, subject to shareholder approval at the 33rd AGM (04th August, 2026). Company maintains a published Dividend Distribution Policy, Risk Management Policy and Directors & Officers Insurance Policy. Mr. Vinod Kumar Gupta was proposed for re-appointment as Managing Director for a further 5-year term (1st September, 2026 to 31st August, 2031); shareholders were asked to pre-approve that aggregate remuneration to promoter Executive Directors may exceed the statutory caps under Sections 196/197 and Schedule V of the Companies Act, 2013 / Regulation 17(6)(e) of SEBI (LODR).
currentContext.expansion: Dollar's capex activity in the AR centres on a renewable-energy roadmap aimed at making its Tirupur spinning unit self-reliant on power. During FY2025-26, the Company installed a 2 MW Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) integrated with its existing solar infrastructure, which stores surplus solar energy and releases it to the grid during peak hours, and expanded its solar power plant by 4 MW, taking total installed solar capacity to 12 MW (alongside 4.95 MW of wind capacity). Two further capital projects are under way under this roadmap, both expected to be commissioned in FY2026-27: a Rooftop Solar Plant of 1.3 MW capacity at the existing manufacturing facility, and a Ground-Mounted Solar Plant of 4 MW capacity at Pudukkottai, to be set up on 11.24 acres of land already acquired for this purpose. A further 2 MW of solar capacity addition is planned for the next fiscal year. A zero-discharge bleaching plant is operational. Separately, 57% of the Company's FY2025-26 capex (vs 0% in FY2024-25) was directed to technologies improving environmental/social impact of products and processes.
currentContext.mdna: Indian innerwear category is shifting from a commodity-led, need-based segment to a brand-driven, comfort-led, premiumising lifestyle category, with consumers seeking better fit, design, quality and brand assurance.|Indian innerwear market valued at approximately US$10.9 billion in 2025, projected to reach US$19.8 billion by 2034 (6.5% annual growth); broader apparel industry expanding at 3.16% average from US$88 billion to a projected US$117.05 billion by 2034 (source: IMARC Group).|Consumers increasingly prioritise performance-led features such as breathability, stretch, ergonomic design and comfort-led construction, benefiting innerwear, athleisure and adjacent comfortwear categories.|India's consumption base remained resilient, supported by formalisation, wider access and a broadening consumer base, though consumers are becoming more selective, expecting better value, quality, comfort and brand assurance.|Force NXT delivered 16.5% value growth and 26.2% volume growth during the year, reinforcing the premiumisation opportunity within the portfolio.|Operating environment remained complex: volatile raw material prices, discounting intensity, cost pressures (cotton, yarn, packaging, energy, logistics) and global trade uncertainty challenged apparel companies during the year.

thesis: Dollar is a distribution-led (87% trade) innerwear branded play executing a volume-growth + distribution-deepening (Project Lakshya) strategy while margins are temporarily pressured by an adverse product mix (economy mix up) and elevated cotton/yarn costs. The reflexive bet: ~4-6% price hikes (industry-wide, first in 2 years), advertising rationalization (A&P to 5.5% of revenue), de-leveraging to zero net debt by FY28, and channel shift to quick-commerce/modern-trade should restore double-digit EBITDA margin and sustain double-digit topline.
scorecard (q4 fy26 vs yoy; full-year fy2:
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Operating Revenue | INR 622 cr | +13.2% | Volume +12.0% YoY in Q4 |
| Gross Profit | INR 174 cr | +6.7% | GM 28.1% (Q4); compressed ~169-170 bps YoY |
| Operating EBITDA | INR 58 cr | +2.0% | Margin 9.3% (Q4) |
| PAT (reported) | INR 33 cr | +11.4% | PAT margin 5.2% (Q4) |
| **FY26 Op. Revenue** | INR 1,881 cr | +10.0% | FY volume +9.8% |
| **FY26 Gross Profit** | INR 622 cr | +9.6% | GM 33.0% (FY) |
| **FY26 Op. EBITDA** | INR 200 cr | +9.3% | Margin 10.6% (FY); mgmt also cited ~10.82% |
| **FY26 PAT** | INR 107 cr | +18.0% | PAT margin 5.7% (FY) |
| Net debt | INR 264 cr (current) | — | Reduced borrowings ~INR50 cr last yr; target 0 by FY28 |
| Operating cash flow (FY) | INR 139 cr | — | OCF/EBITDA = 70%; cash conv cycle 154 days (FY26) vs 160 (FY25) |

**One-offs / clean-up:** GM compression is mix + input-cost driven (NOT discounting-led, per mgmt). Pepe JV top-line NOT consolidated (only bottom-line). No major one-off in PAT flagged. Dividend INR3/share (payout 15.8%).
guidance (critical):
- **Growth:** No firm FY27 number yet — to be given at Q1 FY27 call. Mgmt "eyeing double-digit growth" in both volume and value; optimistic on strong volume growth. (When pushed on low-teens vs 15%+, declined to specify.)
- **Margin:** FY27 EBITDA margin expected **better than FY26** ("definitely better"). Gross margin expected to improve as price hikes flow through. Double-digit EBITDA margin (already ~10.6% FY; was ~11% historically) expected to hold/improve.
- **Premiumization:** Force NXT growing 25-26% YoY; expected to continue scaling.
- **Distribution:** Project Lakshya Phase 2 pilot launched (deepen active retailers in "gold states"); modern-trade growth targeted **20-25%** this fiscal.
- **Price hikes:** ~3-4% in April + 2-3% in June (total **4-6%**, all-inclusive of scheme/discount, pure price). CFO separately cited ~6-7% in the quarter. First industry hike in ~2 years; no further hikes expected as cotton/yarn stabilizing.
- **De-leverage:** Net debt to ~0 by FY28; cash conversion cycle to improve another 5-7 days in FY27 (mainly receivable days).
demand:
- Underlying demand "intact" but Q4 retail footfall reduced slightly due to **exceptional heat** — flagged as a timing, not structural, issue. Innerwear = "second skin," basic non-discretionary.
- Q4 seasonally strong: distributors stock up ahead of summer + Eid/Holi festivity offtake.
- Q1 typically sees higher consumer buying (summer wear-and-tear; vest used as outerwear by rural/farm consumers).
- No demand hit observed from April price hike (distributors/retailers view price hikes positively).
segment (economy / premium / women's):
- **Economy (Dollar Always/Lehar):** FY26 contribution 41.5% (vs 39.1% FY25); Q4 economy mix rose 45%→47%. Driver = high consumption in Tier 2/3 & semi-rural/rural + unorganized→organized shift + 3 yrs of economy advertising (Saif Ali Khan ambassador for Dollar Lehar). Mgmt insists NOT down-trading ("very rare").
- **Mid-premium / Dollar Man (Bigboss):** FY26 contribution 36.5% (vs 38.8% FY25) — share dipped as economy grew faster. Bigboss anchors at 36.5%, Regular 41.5% (brand-architecture view).
- **Super-premium Force NXT:** +16.0% value / +24.3% volume in Q4; FY +16.5% value / +26.2% volume; contribution 4.5% (vs 4.2% FY25).
- **Women's (Missy / Dollar Woman):** contribution 7.5% (vs 8.0% FY25). Leggings/churidar de-growing ~2 yrs; pant sales rising; lingerie/intimate-wear growing at industry rates. Hopeful for outer-garment growth in FY27.
- **Thermals:** 6.1% (vs 5.9%). **Dollar Protect (rainwear):** Q4 volume +49.9%, FY +18%; contribution 2.1%. **Socks:** 1.6%. Champion 0.1%, Pepe ~0.01%, Force Gowear minimal.
growth / optionality:
- **Quick-commerce:** +437% YoY, contribution 0.5%→2.5%. Non-traditional channels (MT + e-com + q-com) +24.2% YoY in FY26. Modern trade/e-com/q-com now ~10% of revenue; channel margins "almost similar" to trade (higher holding cost offset by faster payments).
- **Project Lakshya:** secondary-sales-based (replenishment, no push). Phase 1 = retailer mapping/enrollment; Phase 2 pilot = deepen active retailers in dominant ("gold") states, remap mature states. New-state entry paused due to aggressive competitor pushback in non-Lakshya states; to resume after Phase 2.
- **Premiumization:** Force NXT super-premium scaling fast; introducing high-EBITDA-margin products.
- **Pepe JV (athleisure innerwear):** D2C / e-com / LFS-only channel; only bottom-line consolidated.
- **Exports:** 3% of sales — Middle East/Gulf, African countries, Southeast Asia (Myanmar/Burma).
- **Multi-brand penetration:** pushing strong distributors of one brand to take on other brands.
margins & cost (cotton / yarn):
- Q4 GM down ~169-170 bps YoY: (1) economy mix up to 47% lowering ASP, (2) rising yarn prices vs flat selling prices compressing realization. NOT discounting-driven.
- Price hikes (4-6%) taken to offset cotton inflation; cotton & yarn prices now "stabilizing."
- A&P rationalized to **5.5% of operating income** in FY26; expected to moderate further on operating leverage.
- Merger of 9 promoter entities to cut RPT — expected ~INR4-5 cr expense reduction (royalty/service charges/rent); minimal revenue impact.
capex: - **No major capex commitments** near term. Garment capacity is job-worker-led (knitting/bleaching/cutting in-house; stitching of economy/mix outsourced); capacity flexible ±20-30% via adding job workers — no capex needed to scale. FY26 volume ~28 crore pieces.
capital allocation:
- Free-cash-flow focus → debt reduction (net debt INR264 cr → 0 by FY28; ~INR130 cr/yr repayment trajectory implied) while funding growth.
- Cash conversion cycle 154 days (FY26) from 160 (FY25); target another 5-7 days down in FY27, mainly receivables.
- Dividend INR3/share, payout 15.8%.
risks:
- **Demand:** heat-driven footfall softness (timing); semi-discretionary but basic.
- **Input cost:** cotton/yarn inflation; further hikes possible if prices don't stabilize.
- **Mix:** continued economy-mix shift dilutes ASP/GM.
- **Competition:** Page/Jockey, Rupa, Lux (not named explicitly but "organized players"); aggressive competitor pushback in non-Lakshya new states; D2C players moving back online (mgmt says miniscule offline impact). Competitive intensity described as "stabilizing."
- **Women's:** structural de-growth in leggings/churidar.
- **Execution:** Lakshya Phase 2 / new-state entry timing uncertain.
mgmt tone: Confident, execution-focused, optimistic on FY27 ("great fiscal year"). Repeatedly deferred firm guidance to Q1 FY27 call. Framed margin pressure as temporary/cyclical, not structural. Multiple audio dropouts during the call (technical glitches noted). CFO answers occasionally garbled ("echo sound").
non-obvious takeaways:
- Pepe JV revenue does NOT flow into reported top-line (only ~bottom-line via 51% JV) — top-line understates the franchise.
- G.O.A.T alliance went 100% D2C; INR49 cr rev, ~10% PAT margin — a profitable digital arm.
- Economy advertising (Saif Ali Khan / Dollar Lehar) is a deliberate 3-yr strategy capturing unorganized→organized shift — economy mix-up is partly self-engineered share gain, not just down-trading.
- Optimal inventory floor is ~95-100 days due to ~90-day production cycle (yarn→finished goods) — structural working-capital floor.
- CFO and President gave slightly different price-hike numbers (4-6% vs 6-7%) — watch realised pricing.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ✅ Quick-commerce/q-com platforms benefit from Dollar's 437% channel ramp (Dollar is the supplier-side beneficiary of q-com proliferation).
- ⭐ Yarn/cotton suppliers benefit from rising yarn demand-supply gap (mgmt cites tight yarn supply).
- (Beneficiaries list for downstream investing left empty — no clear third-party listed beneficiary called out.)

FY26: Rev INR1,881 cr (+10%), EBITDA INR200 cr (10.6%), PAT INR107 cr (+18%). GM compressed ~169 bps YoY on economy mix-up (45%→47%) + yarn cost. Price hikes 4-6% (Apr+Jun); first in 2 yrs. themes.title: Branded innerwear & domestic apparel
themes.need: Branded innerwear and domestic apparel are driven by rural recovery, GST 2.0 and distribution reach - a domestic-consumption thesis, not the China+1/FTA export tailwind powering exporters and synthetics.
themes.driver: Rural recovery + GST 2.0 demand pull and distribution-led volume growth.

hero.oneLiner: A 52-year-old multi-brand Indian hosiery and apparel company (innerwear, outerwear, athleisure, thermals, rainwear) with ~15% share of the Indian hosiery market and one of the industry's widest distribution networks.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: A 52-year-old multi-brand Indian hosiery and apparel company (innerwear, outerwear, athleisure, thermals, rainwear) with ~15% share of the Indian hosiery market and one of the industry's widest distribution networks.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Dollar Industries Limited, founded in 1972, has grown into a leading Indian hosiery and apparel company manufacturing and selling innerwear, outerwear, athleisure, thermals, rainwear and comfortwear for men, women and children under a multi-brand portfolio (Dollar Man, Dollar Woman, Dollar Junior, Force NXT, Pepe Jeans innerwear JV, among others). Products reach consumers through general trade, large-format stores, exclusive brand outlets, e-commerce, quick-commerce and exports to 15 countries, serving both B2B (dealers, distributors, wholesalers, retailers, institutions) and B2C customers.

segment_detail.title: Segment (economy / premium / women's)
segment_detail.body:
- **Economy (Dollar Always/Lehar):** FY26 contribution 41.5% (vs 39.1% FY25); Q4 economy mix rose 45%→47%. Driver = high consumption in Tier 2/3 & semi-rural/rural + unorganized→organized shift + 3 yrs of economy advertising (Saif Ali Khan ambassador for Dollar Lehar). Mgmt insists NOT down-trading ("very rare").
- **Mid-premium / Dollar Man (Bigboss):** FY26 contribution 36.5% (vs 38.8% FY25) — share dipped as economy grew faster. Bigboss anchors at 36.5%, Regular 41.5% (brand-architecture view).
- **Super-premium Force NXT:** +16.0% value / +24.3% volume in Q4; FY +16.5% value / +26.2% volume; contribution 4.5% (vs 4.2% FY25).
- **Women's (Missy / Dollar Woman):** contribution 7.5% (vs 8.0% FY25). Leggings/churidar de-growing ~2 yrs; pant sales rising; lingerie/intimate-wear growing at industry rates. Hopeful for outer-garment growth in FY27.
- **Thermals:** 6.1% (vs 5.9%). **Dollar Protect (rainwear):** Q4 volume +49.9%, FY +18%; contribution 2.1%. **Socks:** 1.6%. Champion 0.1%, Pepe ~0.01%, Force Gowear minimal.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)
guidance.body:
- **Growth:** No firm FY27 number yet — to be given at Q1 FY27 call. Mgmt "eyeing double-digit growth" in both volume and value; optimistic on strong volume growth. (When pushed on low-teens vs 15%+, declined to specify.)
- **Margin:** FY27 EBITDA margin expected **better than FY26** ("definitely better"). Gross margin expected to improve as price hikes flow through. Double-digit EBITDA margin (already ~10.6% FY; was ~11% historically) expected to hold/improve.
- **Premiumization:** Force NXT growing 25-26% YoY; expected to continue scaling.
- **Distribution:** Project Lakshya Phase 2 pilot launched (deepen active retailers in "gold states"); modern-trade growth targeted **20-25%** this fiscal.
- **Price hikes:** ~3-4% in April + 2-3% in June (total **4-6%**, all-inclusive of scheme/discount, pure price). CFO separately cited ~6-7% in the quarter. First industry hike in ~2 years; no further hikes expected as cotton/yarn stabilizing.
- **De-leverage:** Net debt to ~0 by FY28; cash conversion cycle to improve another 5-7 days in FY27 (mainly receivable days).

growth_optionality.title: Growth / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Quick-commerce:** +437% YoY, contribution 0.5%→2.5%. Non-traditional channels (MT + e-com + q-com) +24.2% YoY in FY26. Modern trade/e-com/q-com now ~10% of revenue; channel margins "almost similar" to trade (higher holding cost offset by faster payments).
- **Project Lakshya:** secondary-sales-based (replenishment, no push). Phase 1 = retailer mapping/enrollment; Phase 2 pilot = deepen active retailers in dominant ("gold") states, remap mature states. New-state entry paused due to aggressive competitor pushback in non-Lakshya states; to resume after Phase 2.
- **Premiumization:** Force NXT super-premium scaling fast; introducing high-EBITDA-margin products.
- **Pepe JV (athleisure innerwear):** D2C / e-com / LFS-only channel; only bottom-line consolidated.
- **Exports:** 3% of sales — Middle East/Gulf, African countries, Southeast Asia (Myanmar/Burma).
- **Multi-brand penetration:** pushing strong distributors of one brand to take on other brands.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian innerwear category is shifting from a commodity-led, need-based segment to a brand-driven, comfort-led, premiumising lifestyle category, with consumers seeking better fit, design, quality and brand assurance.
- Indian innerwear market valued at approximately US$10.9 billion in 2025, projected to reach US$19.8 billion by 2034 (6.5% annual growth); broader apparel industry expanding at 3.16% average from US$88 billion to a projected US$117.05 billion by 2034 (source: IMARC Group).
- Consumers increasingly prioritise performance-led features such as breathability, stretch, ergonomic design and comfort-led construction, benefiting innerwear, athleisure and adjacent comfortwear categories.
- India's consumption base remained resilient, supported by formalisation, wider access and a broadening consumer base, though consumers are becoming more selective, expecting better value, quality, comfort and brand assurance.
- Force NXT delivered 16.5% value growth and 26.2% volume growth during the year, reinforcing the premiumisation opportunity within the portfolio.
- Operating environment remained complex: volatile raw material prices, discounting intensity, cost pressures (cotton, yarn, packaging, energy, logistics) and global trade uncertainty challenged apparel companies during the year.

margins.title: Margins & cost (cotton / yarn)
margins.body:
- Q4 GM down ~169-170 bps YoY: (1) economy mix up to 47% lowering ASP, (2) rising yarn prices vs flat selling prices compressing realization. NOT discounting-driven.
- Price hikes (4-6%) taken to offset cotton inflation; cotton & yarn prices now "stabilizing."
- A&P rationalized to **5.5% of operating income** in FY26; expected to moderate further on operating leverage.
- Merger of 9 promoter entities to cut RPT — expected ~INR4-5 cr expense reduction (royalty/service charges/rent); minimal revenue impact.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Free-cash-flow focus → debt reduction (net debt INR264 cr → 0 by FY28; ~INR130 cr/yr repayment trajectory implied) while funding growth.
- Cash conversion cycle 154 days (FY26) from 160 (FY25); target another 5-7 days down in FY27, mainly receivables.
- Dividend INR3/share, payout 15.8%.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Dollar's capex activity in the AR centres on a renewable-energy roadmap aimed at making its Tirupur spinning unit self-reliant on power. During FY2025-26, the Company installed a 2 MW Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) integrated with its existing solar infrastructure, which stores surplus solar energy and releases it to the grid during peak hours, and expanded its solar power plant by 4 MW, taking total installed solar capacity to 12 MW (alongside 4.95 MW of wind capacity). Two further capital projects are under way under this roadmap, both expected to be commissioned in FY2026-27: a Rooftop Solar Plant of 1.3 MW capacity at the existing manufacturing facility, and a Ground-Mounted Solar Plant of 4 MW capacity at Pudukkottai, to be set up on 11.24 acres of land already acquired for this purpose. A further 2 MW of solar capacity addition is planned for the next fiscal year. A zero-discharge bleaching plant is operational. Separately, 57% of the Company's FY2025-26 capex (vs 0% in FY2024-25) was directed to technologies improving environmental/social impact of products and processes.

management_tone.title: Mgmt tone
management_tone.body: Confident, execution-focused, optimistic on FY27 ("great fiscal year"). Repeatedly deferred firm guidance to Q1 FY27 call. Framed margin pressure as temporary/cyclical, not structural. Multiple audio dropouts during the call (technical glitches noted). CFO answers occasionally garbled ("echo sound").

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Backward integration from fibre to fashion across yarn, fabric and elastic manufacturing, giving control over quality, cost and input volatility and reducing vendor dependence.
- Multi-brand portfolio spanning value-led everyday essentials (Dollar Always, Dollar Man) to premium/lifestyle lines (Force NXT, Pepe Jeans innerwear JV), enabling participation across price points, seasons and lifestyles.
- Pan-India distribution network of 1,500+ dealers, 145,000+ retail outlets, 1,024 large-format-store presence and 1,500+ dark-store presence via quick-commerce platforms - one of the widest in the industry.
- Brand ambassador equity (Akshay Kumar - Bigboss, Saif Ali Khan - Lehar, Yami Gautam - Missy, Mahesh Babu - Bigboss South India) supporting consumer recall across regions and demographics.
- Project Lakshya distribution-intelligence programme (retailer mapping, digital enrolment, geo-tagging, distributor tracking) shifting the Company from a push-led to a replenishment-led, demand-responsive distribution system; covers 319 Lakshya distributors contributing 30.4% of revenue across 14 states.

risks.title: Risks
risks.body:
- **Demand:** heat-driven footfall softness (timing); semi-discretionary but basic.
- **Input cost:** cotton/yarn inflation; further hikes possible if prices don't stabilize.
- **Mix:** continued economy-mix shift dilutes ASP/GM.
- **Competition:** Page/Jockey, Rupa, Lux (not named explicitly but "organized players"); aggressive competitor pushback in non-Lakshya new states; D2C players moving back online (mgmt says miniscule offline impact). Competitive intensity described as "stabilizing."
- **Women's:** structural de-growth in leggings/churidar.
- **Execution:** Lakshya Phase 2 / new-state entry timing uncertain.

strategy.body:

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Scheme of Arrangement] A proposed merger of nine promoter group companies into Dollar Industries — ADDS Projects, Dindayal Texpro (de-merged segment), Amicable Properties, Bhawani Yarns, Dollar Brands, Goldman Trading, KPS Distributors, PHPL Properties and Zest Merchants — aimed at strengthening in-house production capacity, reducing intercompany transactions and avoiding conflict of interest.

Ltd. owns the 'Dollar' trademark), manufacturing & job work (Dindayal Texpro, Bhawani Yarns) and real estate leasing (Goldman Trading, ADDS Projects, Amicable Properties, KPS Distributors, PHPL Properties, Zest Merchants).

Ltd.; G.O.A.T acquired 50% stake of Pepe plus an additional 2% non-voting equity, and would undertake business operations as a multi-brand distributor, with expected outcomes of D2C supply, inorganic growth/brand acquisition and a foothold in super premium brands.
